extracted.intended_audience: aspiring fiction writers, especially short-story authors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and checklist for crafting and revising short fiction, emphasizing a single, tightly-focused narrative with strong character desire, conflict, and a resonant ending. Covers elements to include, revision targets, and short-story-specific constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protagonist with desire/need
rubrics_metrics.description: Protagonist must want something they don't have, to drive story forward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The character's desire or need should be the engine of the story—clear motivation that creates stakes and propels action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear dilemma
rubrics_metrics.description: A clear dilemma presented with minimal backstory; focus on how the dilemma is resolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit setup; concentrate the narrative energy on the dilemma and its resolution rather than long exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisive action
rubrics_metrics.description: What does the protagonist do about the dilemma?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The story should show the protagonist taking action (not just thinking) that advances or resolves the central conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting, plot, POV
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic fiction elements (setting, plot, point of view) must be present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure these core elements are clear and serve the story—POV should be consistent and setting should support mood and character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single central storyline
rubrics_metrics.description: One central storyline only—no subplots (those push toward novella).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid secondary plots that dilute focus; keep narrative scope tight and concentrated on the main arc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Each word essential
rubrics_metrics.description: Every word in the story should be essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cut unnecessary words, redundancies, and filler; prefer economical language that serves scene, voice, or tension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Each scene ramps up tension
rubrics_metrics.description: Every scene should increase stakes or tension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eliminate scenes that do not advance conflict or deepen character; each scene must push the narrative forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Each character clearly defined
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters must be distinct and clearly defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give characters clear desires, voices, and traits; avoid interchangeable or background characters that add no function.

rubrics_metrics.name: No exposition dumps
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid exposition dumps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reveal backstory and necessary information through action, dialogue, and detail rather than large blocks of explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialogue distinct per character
rubrics_metrics.description: Dialogue should be distinct for each character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use voice, diction, and syntax to differentiate speakers; avoid giving all characters the same rhythm or phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opening hook is in place
rubrics_metrics.description: The opening must hook the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with an element that promises conflict or curiosity; the opening should signal what the story will deliver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ending is earned, not arbitrary
rubrics_metrics.description: Ending must feel earned rather than arbitrary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The resolution should follow logically from character choices and story events; aim for an ending that feels inevitable in retrospect yet may surprise in the moment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot (with conflict)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plot must exist and include conflict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Central conflict drives plot—ensure cause-and-effect progression rather than episodic scenes without stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character
rubrics_metrics.description: Character is a core element (well-drawn, with desires and needs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize compelling inner life and motivations that justify actions and invite reader investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Setting is a key element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use setting to enhance mood, complicate the plot, or reveal character; avoid irrelevant descriptive detours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theme
rubrics_metrics.description: Story should have a theme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theme emerges from the choices characters make and the consequences; avoid heavy-handed moralizing—let theme arise naturally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point of View
rubrics_metrics.description: Point of view is essential and must be controlled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select and maintain a POV that best serves intimacy and focus; for short stories, tighter POV (often one character) is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Tone should be consistent and appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a tonal throughline (serious, comic, ironic, etc.) that supports scene choices and voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorial style must suit the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Style includes sentence rhythm, diction, and narrative manner—choose stylistic choices that enhance clarity and mood without drawing undue attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mood
rubrics_metrics.description: Mood should be established and sustained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use imagery, pacing, and detail to create emotional atmosphere appropriate to the story's aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tight POV (usually one character)
rubrics_metrics.description: Short stories should usually use a tight POV—often one character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single, focused perspective intensifies immediacy and helps maintain narrative compression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single time frame / compressed timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a single time frame or a compressed timeline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit temporal scope to keep momentum and avoid the sprawling chronology typical of longer forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: One major reversal
rubrics_metrics.description: Include one major reversal in the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A decisive turning point or twist provides dramatic payoff; avoid multiple reversals that complicate short-form clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resonant ending; ambiguity over tidy resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim for a resonant ending—ambiguity is often more powerful than tidy resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trust the reader to infer consequences; favor emotional resonance or thematic closure over exhaustive plot wrap-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title as commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: Title can act as commentary on the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a title that adds layer or irony, or frames reader expectations without spoon-feeding meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opening must promise what the story delivers
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the opening promise something the story delivers?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The premise or emotional promise in the opening should be paid off by the story's development and ending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early, clear inciting incident
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the inciting incident clear and early?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present the event that sets the central conflict in motion promptly so the story can focus on consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Every scene serves central conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: Does every scene serve the central conflict?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove or revise scenes that don't advance plot, deepen character, or raise stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cut added explanation/justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Have you cut all explanation/justification added in draft?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During revision, eliminate writerly rationalizations and trust the story—avoid sentences that explain why characters act instead of showing it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ending: inevitable in retrospect, surprising in the moment
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the ending inevitable in retrospect, surprising in the moment?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance surprise with logical consequence—readers should feel the ending fits even if it astonishes them.
